scenarios.purpose: Explain a proposed self-service request submission and own-request tracking capability.
scenarios.journey: SYNTHETIC requester submits their own request, checks status, and never sees another requester's data. Triage assesses intake; business roles do not grant Odoo access.
sow_narrative: Requesters and triage benefit from own-request submission and tracking.
Include own submission/tracking and isolation; exclude delegated submission, billing and deployment.
D1 is the submission/tracking design; evaluate FR1, FR2 and cross-cutting NFR1.
Discover requester authority, review design, run negative identity experiments, and hand over design evidence.
The scope owner clarifies delegation; delivery authors design and evaluation evidence. No implicit customer obligation.
Delegation authority is unknown; company/project isolation is required; actual hosting is outside this fixture.
Named scope owner evaluates explicit requirement expectations and synthetic verification references; Task Done is insufficient.
Delegation is excluded by DEC1; any later inclusion needs separate scope-change approval.
No commercial arrangement asserted. Optional reference: synthetic://portal/commercial-discussion-not-agreed.
SOW and detailed spec have separately recorded exact internal approvals, not legal signatures.

deliverable.text: Request submission and own-request tracking design

requirements.text: A requester can submit a request for themselves.
requirements.verification: Demonstrate valid own submission and reject a forged requester

requirements.text: A requester can track only their own requests.
requirements.rationale: Useful tracking without another requester's disclosure
requirements.verification: Two requesters attempt list, direct-ID and export access

requirements.text: Project and company boundaries must not leak requests or request metadata.
requirements.verification: Negative identity/project/company tests with zero leaked names/counts

questions.text: Who may submit on behalf of another requester?
questions.resolution: Delegation excluded from initial scope; future discovery remains open

decisions.choice: Exclude delegated submission from initial scope
decisions.consequences: Own requests only; later scope approval required for delegation

weaknesses: Requester/delegation semantics need actual customer discovery
Native Project portal sharing is NOT proof of own-request isolation
Task Done alone cannot satisfy requirement acceptance

scenarios.purpose: Discover an unknown interface before agreeing integration scope.
scenarios.journey: SYNTHETIC operator requests evidence from an external interface owner and reviews a discovery Spike; schema and replay behavior remain unverified.
sow_narrative: Help the operator and interface owner discover evidence before a delivery commitment.
Include interface discovery only; exclude implementation commitments, credentials and invented API behavior.
D1 contains discovery findings; evaluate authoritative direction/schema and replay evidence, not assumed compatibility.
Run an explicit discovery Spike, review evidence, then propose separately approved scope and spec successors.
An internal owner requests information; an external-owner narrative records the missing source. No automatic account creation.
Authentication, limits, schema and idempotency are unresolved dependencies; none is an established fact.
The scope owner evaluates supplied discovery evidence. No integration acceptance is asserted by this fixture.
DEC1 defers delivery. The inbound-only revision is hypothetical and needs separate approvals.
No pricing/payment commitment; optional reference synthetic://integration/discovery-discussion-not-agreed.
Record discovery SOW approval separately from the solution spec; unresolved questions remain visible.

requirements.text: Proposed exchange direction is pending interface discovery.
requirements.verification: Unverified: owner must provide authoritative direction/schema

requirements.text: Proposed retries must avoid duplicate business effects.
requirements.verification: Pending authoritative replay contract and duplicate experiment

questions.text: What schema, authentication, limits and replay guarantees actually exist?

decisions.consequences: No invented API or automatic delivery estimate

reviewed_scope_revision.text: SYNTHETIC branch: after evidence, propose inbound-only reconciliation
reviewed_scope_revision.decision_context: Hypothetical discovery branch, not observed external behavior
reviewed_scope_revision.consequences: Old Spike link stays FR1@1; no automatic relink

weaknesses: Scope revision is a labeled hypothetical acceptance input
Discovery completion does not approve delivery scope

scenarios.purpose: Start from an internal solution brief and preserve existing backlog planning.
scenarios.journey: SYNTHETIC internal operator inspects authorized project status, while a product owner manually chooses a delivery slice and keeps maintenance work distinct. No SOW is required.

requirements.text: An operator can inspect operations status in their authorized project.
requirements.verification: Authorized status view; foreign-project direct ID denied

requirements.text: Company and Project isolation applies to all operations views and exports.
requirements.verification: Single/multiple enabled companies, hidden project and export matrix

questions.text: Which existing Sprint will deliberately take the next delivery slice?

decisions.choice: Use an internal brief and existing planning
decisions.consequences: No SOW prerequisite; Sprint selection remains manual

tasks.name: SYNTHETIC maintenance: refresh development dependencies
tasks.maintenance_reason: Development maintenance, not missing functional coverage

planning.surface: Existing Agile backlog and optional native Scrum
planning.expectation: Sprint event retains v1; current Task link may deliberately move to v2

weaknesses: Maintenance must be distinguishable from unexplained unlinked work
SOW absence must not bypass spec approval
Frozen Sprint context cannot be derived from current links
